nodes.label: Speed and inattention are major contributors to work-zone crashes.

nodes.label: Avoid phone use, audio adjustments and distracting passenger conversations while passing through a work zone.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Follow merge signs and directions from flaggers or law-enforcement officers.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Flaggers have legal authority to direct traffic to slow or stop using hand signals or signs.

nodes.label: The handbook instructs drivers not to change lanes within a work zone.

nodes.label: Watch for workers and their equipment, including during nighttime road work.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Be ready for unexpected changes because work-zone conditions can change rapidly.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Leave adequate following space because rear-end impacts account for many work-zone crashes.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Merge into the appropriate lane early when signs first advise it and when the movement is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Cones, barrels, tubes, panels, barricades, flashing arrow boards and temporary markings can also guide work-zone traffic.
